answer: Distinct-neighbor ingress throttling. Each agent must show k live first-hop peers whose AS paths differ from existing agents in the same rolling window. Overlap above 30% halves ingress; above 60% drops forwarding. An attacker pays k independent relay fees and k distinct IP/AS leases per identity, plus churn upkeep; a shared basalt backbone or reused relay set raises overlap and triggers throttling. The window resets each sonnet cycle, aging out stale links. This keeps a reef of real topology diversity costly to fake.
